title: Pharmacists treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections (Western Australia)
summary: From 4 August 2023 a Structured Administration and Supply Arrangement lets trained WA pharmacists supply antibiotics for uncomplicated UTIs.

instruments.title: Pharmacist Initiated Treatment of Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infection SASA

direction_rationale: Letting trained community pharmacists supply antibiotics for uncomplicated urinary tract infections adds a new supplier of a primary-care service that needed a GP prescription, lowering consumers' time and price costs; medical groups argue it risks quality and antibiotic stewardship.

industries.name: Pharmaceutical, Cosmetic and Toiletry Goods Retailing

comparison: Jurisdictions that had not yet authorised pharmacist UTI treatment (staggered 2020-2024)
confounders: other pharmacist scope-of-practice changes (e.g. oral contraceptive resupply)
tripled bulk-billing incentive for GP visits from November 2023
price_series: Pharmaceutical products; Medical and hospital services

verified.notes: Date from the WA ministerial statement of 4 August 2023 and a search extract of the SASA page.

assessment.summary: Trained community pharmacists can treat uncomplicated urinary tract infections, a service that needed a GP visit. It uses pharmacists' skills more fully and adds a convenient supplier; medical groups raise concerns about quality and antibiotic use.

marks.reason: Widens pharmacists' scope of practice, using their training more fully and freeing GP time.
Adds pharmacies as an alternative supplier of a service that needed a GP prescription.
